targetName: Machinist Bench Vise with Swivel Base

objectClass.primaryType: machinist bench vise with swivel base
objectClass.notes: Bare ferrous metal workholding clamp, bilaterally symmetric about the vertical plane containing the screw axis. Four macro assemblies: swivel base, body casting with the fixed jaw, movable jaw on a slide bar, lead screw with a ball-ended T-handle. Two real kinematic degrees of freedom are visible in the reference: the jaw translates along the screw axis and the whole body swivels about the base axis; the handle bar slides and the screw rotates. No paint, no decal, no dielectric surface anywhere.

reasoning: Silhouette is interrupted at three places by real negative space (the jaw gap, the gap under the exposed screw run, the gap between base lobes) — a single hull cannot produce it.
Four macro assemblies decompose into ~16 visible sub-parts; the movable jaw alone is arm + slide bar + thrust lobe + jaw plate.
Hierarchy is genuinely three deep: base -> body -> fixed jaw arm -> jaw plate -> serration row.
Repetition is dense and identity-defining: two helical thread runs (~29 visible turns combined), an axial knurl band, two serration rows, four base lobes, four hex fasteners.
Four distinct machining finishes share one metal family: rough casting, machined stock, dark-oxide screw, near-polished handle.
Occlusion risk is moderate: the entire rear half, the base underside and both internal channels are unseen and reconstructed by symmetry/convention.
Action readiness is high — the reference object is a mechanism, so jaw travel, body swivel, screw spin and handle slide all need real pivots and limits.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Chosen from the observed structure: multi-assembly mechanism, dense helical/knurl/serration repetition, four finish variants of one metal family, and two real kinematic axes. Not ultra-complex: there is no organic surface, no pattern finish, no wear layer and no text/marking to match.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Rear (-Z) half of every casting is unseen; reconstructed by mirroring the observed +Z half.
Base underside, nut-boss interior and slide-channel interior are never visible; built to engineering convention.
Jaw-plate serration pitch and count are below reliable count resolution in the reference; pitch approximated.
Whether the chamfered body plateau is a true flat anvil pad or only a cast chamfer.
Whether all four base lobes carry fasteners or only the two visible front lobes.
Absolute scale carries no cue in the reference; a conventional 125 mm jaw width is adopted and every dimension expressed relative to it.
Exact thread pitch counted from the render with +/-2 turns of uncertainty.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.note: Horizontal rows of triangular gripping teeth across both jaw faces; teeth run across the jaw width, plate stands proud of the arm.
Each jaw plate carries a small stepped tab standing above the arm's top edge — a strong silhouette cue at the top of the jaw gap.
Trapezoidal (acme) thread, two exposed runs: a long run between body face and movable jaw, a short tail past the -X body face. Crest line is the brightest specular in that zone.
Fine axial knurl ridges around the thrust ring between the movable jaw lobe and the handle; reads as a dense vertical hatch.
Every casting edge is filleted, never sharp; the inner scallop of each jaw arm meets its top face through a broad fillet.
The body's top plateau behind the fixed jaw is bounded by a hard chamfer that catches a bright grazing rim line.
Both exposed screw ends are chamfered rather than square-cut.
Hex bolt heads seated in the front base lobes; hexagonal head, raised, machined finish brighter than the casting around it.
Single hex-headed swivel lock bolt on the front of the swivel collar.
Small hex fastener boss on the lower front face of the body casting near the swivel.
Through mounting holes centred in each radial base lobe; counterbored mouth.
A crisp circular parting seam separates the swivel collar from the fixed foot disc — a recessed groove plus a darker crevice, not a painted line.
The slide bar exits the body through a rectangular guide mouth; the gap around it reads as a dark recessed seam.
The two handle balls carry the tightest, brightest specular lobes in the reference — the lowest roughness in the whole object.
Low-amplitude mottled roughness/tone variation over every cast surface (sand-cast grain), absent from machined and turned surfaces.

definitionOfDone: Rendered silhouette reproduces the reference's three negative spaces: the jaw gap, the gap beneath the exposed mid screw run, and the gaps between base lobes.
Both jaw arms show the hooked profile — convex outer face, deep concave inner scallop, broad fillet at the top — not a plain rectangular upright.
Two separate exposed thread runs are present with visible helical relief, not a smooth cylinder and not a texture.
Longitudinal proportions match the reference: overall width : height ~2.25:1, base disc diameter ~0.42 x overall width, jaw opening ~0.17 x overall width.
Four finish variants of one metal family are distinguishable in the render: rough casting, machined stock, dark-oxide screw, near-polished handle.
The T-handle reads as a straight bar with a sphere at each end, cross-drilled through the screw head and free to slide.
Model is explodable and clickable, and the two real kinematic axes (jaw travel, body swivel) are driveable with limits.

featureGroups.name: Hooked jaw-arm profile and jaw gap
qualityCriteria: Both arms are built from an extruded profile whose outer face is convex and whose inner face is a deep concave scallop closing to a broad top fillet.
The jaws oppose along the screw axis and the open gap between the jaw faces equals the exposed mid screw run to within 15%.
Each arm's top carries a serrated plate standing proud of the arm face with a stepped tab above the arm's top edge.
failureModes: arms modelled as plain rectangular uprights, losing the reference's most recognizable outline
jaw plates flush with the arm instead of standing proud
serrations painted rather than built as geometry

featureGroups.name: Lead screw, two exposed thread runs and the nut boss
qualityCriteria: Thread is real swept helical geometry with a trapezoidal (acme) section, not a cylinder with a striped material.
Two exposed runs exist: the long run between the body face and the movable jaw, and the short tail past the -X body face.
Thread pitch is constant across both runs and the runs share one axis with the slide.
failureModes: smooth cylinder standing in for the thread
thread run only on one side of the body
screw axis not collinear with the slide axis, so jaw travel skews

featureGroups.name: Four-lobed swivel base with parting seam
qualityCriteria: Base is a radially repeated system: four lobes on a common disc, each with a counterbored through hole.
A crisp circular parting seam separates the swivel collar from the fixed foot disc, built as recessed geometry.
Hex-headed fasteners are instanced, not modelled one by one.
failureModes: plain cylindrical base with no lobes
seam faked as a dark line with no relief
lobes at irregular angles instead of a 90-degree radial system

featureGroups.name: Knurled thrust ring and ball-ended T-handle
qualityCriteria: Knurl band is geometric relief around the thrust ring, dense enough to read as a hatch at the review distance.
Handle is one straight bar with a sphere at each end, passing through a cross hole in the screw head.
The handle balls carry the lowest roughness in the scene and the tightest specular lobes.
failureModes: knurling as a roughness map only
handle balls fused into the bar with no neck
handle modelled as an L instead of a through-bar

featureGroups.name: Four machining finishes within one metal family
qualityCriteria: Castings, machined stock, dark-oxide screw and polished handle are separable by eye in the render.
Roughness carries the separation, not albedo alone; all four stay metalness 1.0.
Cast surfaces carry low-amplitude mottled roughness variation absent from machined surfaces.
failureModes: one grey metal everywhere, so the object reads as a single injection-moulded part
albedo used as the roughness signal

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Overall width : height ~2.25:1 with the screw axis horizontal.
Base disc diameter ~0.42 x overall width; the body casting mass sits centred over it.
All three reference negative spaces survive at review distance.
failureModes: model reads as a generic clamp instead of this vise
proportions guessed rather than measured off the reference silhouette

visualDeltaChecks: silhouette and negative-space delta (jaw gap, under-screw gap, inter-lobe gaps)
thread pitch, run length and helix direction delta
base lobe count, radial spacing and seam depth delta
roughness separation delta across the four finish variants
handle bar tilt and ball diameter delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
